newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-SRI LANKA SINK TO 2-0 LOSS VS NEW ZEALAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA SINK TO 2-0 LOSS VS NEW ZEALAND.

text.p: Precisely a year after their dazzling victory in cricket's World Cup, Sri Lanka sank on Monday to a 2-0 test series loss to New Zealand, ranked bottom of the table of test-playing nations.
Set 326 to win the second test, and already in trouble at 20 for two overnight, Sri Lanka never looked like achieving the target on a difficult wicket.
They fell 120 runs short when they were bowled out for 205 with more than a day to spare.
For New Zealand it was a triumph for youth -- for 23-year-old Stephen Fleming, the country's youngest captain, and 18-year-old left-arm spinner Daniel Vettori, who was man of the match.
He spearheaded the victory with five for 84 and won his match award with a total of nine wickets for the test.

Only a bizarre umpiring decision deprived him of a 10-wicket haul. He bowled Kumar Dharmasena but Pakistani umpire Mahboob Shah, confused by wicketkeeper Adam Parore taking off the other bail, ruled the batsman not out.
For New Zealand, the victory was a further step in a remarkable renaissance during their summer home series.
They lost a test series against England 2-0 and were down 2-0 in the five match one-day series against the same opponents before squaring it 2-2, tying one game and winning the last two.
Then captain Lee Germon was sacked and New Zealand went on to win the first test against Sri Lanka by an innings -- followed up by Monday's emphatic second test win.
For New Zealand it was the first home series win since beating Zimbabwe in 1990 and the first time they had won back-to-back tests since against Pakistan in 1985.
Vettori got excellent support from seamer Simon Doull, who finished with three for 43 and first innings destroyer, speedster Heath Davis, with one for 35.
Nightwatchman Chaminda Vaas stuck around for 41 minutes in the morning before his impatience saw him loft Vettori to Dipak Patel when on eight.

Doull then struck a big blow by trapping leading Sri Lankan batsman Aravinda de Silva leg before wicket for five -- his fourth failure of the series -- to have the tourists precariously placed at 50 for four.
The only real Sri Lankan resistance came in a defiant fifth-wicket stand of 79 between adhesive opening batsman Roshan Mahanama and captain Arjuna Ranatunga which carried the tourists to 129.
But they were parted after 100 minutes when Ranatunga, who had used all of his vast experience to reach 33, swept Vettori directly to Doull behind square leg.

Wicketkeeper Romesh Kaluwitharana was gone 18 runs later when Doull trapped him leg before. He then dismissed Roshan Mahanama in similar fashion, ending his fighting innings of 65 after more than four hours.
Nuwan Zoysa hit three boundaries in quick time before he became Vettori's fourth wicket when an attempted sweep shot saw the ball balloon gently to wicketkeeper Adam Parore.
Dharmasena, who made 38 not out despite being bowled, made the most of his life and kept hitting out, but the end was inevitable.

Davis had Sajeewa de Silva for a duck and then fittingly, Vettori finished off the test when Muttiah Muralitharan spooned at catch to Chris Cairns in the deep to give him his first five-wicket bag in only his fourth test.
The teams begin a three-match one-day series on Saturday.
